mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accommodative monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and typically produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low-rate periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.3 percentage points over a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate profit growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, or the signal's Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) over the prior 3 months indicates weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline in the prior 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the joint signal's Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high industrial production growth (INDPRO > 102 and rising), manufacturing output expansion signals robust corporate earnings, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO > 102, or the signal's Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly growth rate in real GDP (GDPC1) signals expanding economic activity, which typically supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in positive GDP growth periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month window signals accelerating inflation, which typically triggers monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp in 3 months, or the signal's Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the prior 3 months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced consumer spending power.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises in the prior 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the joint signal's Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0), the Federal Reserve's rate hikes typically cause a contraction in liquidity and a shift to risk-off sentiment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0, or the signal's Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.
